correctness.rationale: Let F~Bin(n,p), g(k)=min(k,h(n−k)), n≥3,h≥2. Discrete slopes of g are nonincreasing with at least one strict decrease, so Bernstein second derivative R″=n(n−1)E Δ²g(Bin(n−2,p))<0 for all 0<p<1 and endpoint slopes have opposite signs. Reflection around p=1/2 shows R′(1/2)>0 exactly for n≥3,h≥2, so unique output optimum p*>1/2 whereas S=1−p^n−(1−p)^n maximizes uniquely at 1/2; boundaries n=2 or h=1 share optimum. Lipschitz binomial concentration gives uniform R/n→min(p,h(1−p)) and linear asymptotic gain. For n divisible h+1, slope jump at q=hn/(h+1) makes exact CDF quantile equation; binomial CLT and quantile inversion prove √n(p0−p*)→(√h/(h+1))Φ⁻¹(h/(h+1)). For h≥n−1, g(k)=k except g(n)=0, so R=np−np^n and p*=n⁻¹/(n−1), giving n(1−p*)~log n and no mating ~1/n. Representative exact n=3,h=2 and finite differences independently checked.
